title: Access Guardrails: Phased Adoption Manual for RBAC v2 and Evidence Export
content:
Purpose:
This manual lays out a pragmatic, low-friction approach to introducing RBAC v2 guardrails and end-to-end evidence export to our downstream SIEM. The goal is to allow applications to opt into stronger authorization constraints and richer audit evidence without destabilizing customer-facing flows or existing entitlement tooling.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: RBAC model changes (attribute tagging + timebound grants), audit log enrichment (entitlement decisions, request context, policy version), evidence automation for compliance sampling, and the SIEM export pipeline shape.
- Non-goals: Replacing legacy entitlement datastore in this phase, full migration of all client services, or mandatory enforcement across all product tiers.

Core principles:
1) Incremental: ship small, reversible phases; avoid big-bang flips.
2) Observable: every decision must produce machine-readable evidence.
3) Safe defaults: new guardrails default to "monitoring only" unless explicitly promoted.
4) Low-latency invariants: audit enrichment should not add >3ms median to request paths.

Definitions (quick):
- Guardrail: a non-blocking or blocking policy applied at request time to restrict access surfaces.
- Evidence bundle: compact JSON record describing the entitlement evaluation and provenance emitted for each authorization decision.
- Epoched policy: a versioned policy artifact referenced by id/hash used to ensure reproducible attestation.

Phased adoption plan (high level):
Phase A — Discovery and telemetry (2-3 sprints)
- Run a configuration-only pilot: instrument 5 internal services to emit evidence bundles in parallel with current logs.
- Deliver an evidence JSON schema v0.1 and a lightweight SDK for Java/Go/Node.
- Success metric: evidence emitted for >80% of pilot requests and parsable by the SIEM ingest dev team.

Phase B — Pilot enforcement (3 sprints)
- Select two low-risk external integrations (billing-read, metadata-read) to enable soft-fail: decisions are logged and surfaced to owners but do not block.
- Add per-route policy version pinning and sampling rate toggles in Console.
- Success metric: owners approve policy coverage and no customer-facing incidents attributable to guardrail logic for 14 days.

Phase C — Controlled enforcement and evidence retention (4-6 sprints)
- Allow teams to flip guardrails from soft-fail -> hard-enforce via the Console with an approval flow.
- Wire evidence export to SIEM with TTL-based retention and fast query indexes.
- Provide audit-export runbook for support and SRE to retrieve compressed evidence bundles for forensics.
- Success metric: 95% compliance for routes that opted into enforcement, <0.1% false-block rate in first 30 days.

Phase D — Org-wide rollout and automation (ongoing)
- Templates for common guardrails, automatic policy drift detection, periodic attestation reports, and retention policy enforcement for regulated customers.

Minimal migration checklist (per service):
- Add evidence SDK integration (trace-id propagation + policy-id field).
- Emit evidence bundle to local logging pipeline (structured JSON).
- Configure service Console flags for sampling and enforcement mode.
- Schedule a canary window and owner signoff.
- Add queries to existing observability dashboards for new fields (policy_version, decision_outcome, matched_conditions).

Audit/Evidence JSON sketch (compact, single-line example):
{
  "ts":"2025-02-08T17:21:03.123Z",
  "request_id":"req_9b2f",
  "actor":"user:alice@example.com",
  "resource":"model:open-inference:v3",
  "action":"create-job",
  "policy_id":"policy_2025_03_hash",
  "policy_rev":"12",
  "decision":"ALLOW|DENY|MONITOR",
  "reason":"matched:role:project-admin;conditions:[ip-allowlist]",
  "evidence_version":"0.1",
  "latency_ms":"2.7"
}
Note: real records are compacted and NDJSON-wrapped in the log forwarder. The fields above are minimal; extended schemas include attrib snapshots, tokenized resource fingerprints, and signing metadata for compliance customers.

SIEM export considerations:
- Export format: NDJSON with per-record minimal fields and a pointer to compressed evidence blobs in object storage for heavy payloads.
- Ingest guarantees: at-least-once but end-to-end deduplication keys (request_id + policy_hash) to prevent noise.
- Rate control: the export pipeline should support sampling with stable hashes to ensure consistent cohorts across time windows.
- Mapping: map decision to SIEM event types (AUTHZ_ALLOW, AUTHZ_DENY, AUTHZ_MONITOR) and enrich with service tags and region.

Evidence automation and sampling policy:
- Sampling tiers: full (100%) for regulated customers, high (10%) for high-risk endpoints, baseline (0.1%) for low-risk routes.
- Automation checks: periodic verification that policy_id on service logs matches the deployed epoched policy referenced in the Console. Alert on mismatch >0.5% of traffic.
- Auto-archive flow: evidence for denied/high-risk events is retained for 180 days by default; others follow customer-configured retention.

Operational playbook excerpts:
- On unexpected deny spikes: 1) flip route to soft-fail, 2) collect evidence bundle for a 1-hour window, 3) run diff against last-stable policy, 4) rollback to previous policy revision if mismatch is root cause.
- On SIEM ingestion failure: 1) fallback to local retention in object store, 2) enqueue re-play job with request window, 3) notify security-observability on-call channel.

Performance and safety constraints:
- Evidence generation path must run as a non-blocking fast path. If SDK latency budget is exceeded, the outcome should be "monitor-late" with the actual decision defaulting to previous model.
- Signing: for compliance customers, evidence bundles must be HMAC-signed with the KMS key and include signer_id.

Policy governance and attestation:
- Every policy change must produce an attestation artifact with author, timestamp, changelist (Jira ID), and a pre-flight test report.
- The Console will expose a policy health dashboard showing coverage, enforcement state, and evidence emission rate.

Acceptance criteria for full rollout:
- Evidence emitted and parsable for 99% of routed requests across pilot services.
- SIEM ingest latency below 60s 95th percentile under normal load.
- No customer-facing regressions in 30-day observation windows following enforcement flips.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: High volume of evidence increases storage costs. Mitigation: tiered sampling and offloading heavy payloads to compressed object storage with pointers in the lightweight NDJSON.
- Risk: Policy overload creates admin complexity. Mitigation: policy templates, recommended guardrail sets, and a policy linter enforced in the Console.

Open questions / next steps:
- Decide canonical key set for dedupe across multi-region exports (candidate: request_id + region + policy_hash).
- Finalize HMAC signing header format for evidence bundles.
- Plan a cross-team runbook drill with SRE, Support, and Security to simulate a bad policy push.

Notes to reviewers:
- This manual intentionally keeps enforcement opt-in for safety. Please review the suggested sampling rates and the evidence schema for privacy concerns (PII redaction must be enforced in SDKs).

---
End of document.
